title: Buildo pipeline step descriptor
description: THE CANONICAL VOCABULARY (Spec 122 ruling R2). This file — not prose — is the single source of truth for the step contract. docs/reports/generated/122-vocabulary.md and Spec 122's menu tables are GENERATED FROM THIS FILE by scripts/violations/schema-to-vocab.mjs. Encodes operator rulings V1-V6 and R6 (2026-08-23). Omission is a build failure; "none" is a legal value that must be written down, per field, not per category. Contract status: v0 — FREEZES AT C3 (after the eighth archetype pilot), never at S1 exit.

x-rulings.V1: identity.archetype uses FULL WORDS; the ING|MAT|... forms are display shorthand only and are not legal values.
x-rulings.V2: identity.lock is unique across manifest UNION one-time/ UNION backfill/ — the wider universe, not the generated registry alone. Cross-file uniqueness is a validator-side check (S2); JSON Schema cannot express it.
x-rulings.V3: guards.schema_drift is none|propagate|pause. 'warn' is DROPPED — a drift response is an action; warn-ness belongs to the orthogonal severity/blocking axes.
x-rulings.V4: outputs.writes[].replay keeps append_unsafe in the enum but BANNED FOR NEW STEPS via x-banned-for-new, so an existing step can still declare its truth.
x-rulings.V5: staleness.pending is DISSOLVED into three axes: scope (which rows) / trigger (what makes the step eligible) / mode_select (what the trigger chooses), plus fingerprint_inputs.
x-rulings.V6: guards.empty_source is the typed form <table> | [<table>,...] | none — AS AMENDED 2026-08-24. The original ruling typed the scalar form only; the array form is a ratified amendment recorded in Spec 122's V-table, needed because a step may guard on more than one source table (enrich_heritage guards on heritage_properties AND heritage_districts, Spec 120 §3.3). Recorded as an amendment rather than restated silently.
x-rulings.R6-acquisition: NOT a category. Absorbed as staleness.trigger[].position (the acquisition lifecycle position) + inputs.reads.externals[].cache.
x-rulings.R6-maintenance: NOT a category. Absorbed as execution.maintenance — declares targets and CONSTRAINS txn_scope (VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction).
x-rulings.R6-terminals: A NEW CATEGORY (the 18th). Declared exit paths, each with its records_meta shape. Retires the hand-written per-terminal 'PASS'.
x-rulings.R6-plan_shape: NOT a category. A checks[].kind value.
x-rulings.R6-source_key_policy: NOT a category. A per-target field: outputs.writes[].source_key_policy.
x-rulings.R6-on_missing: guards.requires[].on_missing is fail|degrade; degrade requires why AND algorithm, because a degraded branch makes outputs.columns a fiction.
x-rulings.V7: DECOUPLE MECHANIC FROM GUARD (operator ruling, 2026-08-24, closing the S1 menu-completeness gap). write_discipline.class names the write MECHANIC only; guardedness is `guard` (is_distinct_from|none, none requires a why and is grandfathered-only), scope is `scope`, retraction is `retract`. The D and H bans are restated as VALIDATOR RULES over those axes — banned-for-new = (insert-only mechanic AND retract:none) and (set-based mechanic AND scope:none) — not as fused class identities.
x-rulings.R6-schema_drift-conditional: guards.schema_drift may be a SCALAR or a CONDITIONAL PER-LAYER ARRAY (the load-zoning.js:405-407 shape: base layers FAIL/pause, non-base WARN/propagate). A scalar cannot express it.
x-rulings.R-T-invariants-plausibility: Spec 124 §2 Rule 13 R-T addendum (2026-08-29), WF2 'The Step Validator, Data-First'. TWO NEW CATEGORIES (19th/20th): invariants[] (single-table, single-step-scoped declarative-SQL data bounds) and plausibility[] (cross-field/zone-aware, may span tables this step does not itself write) — both executed generically by scripts/lib/step/plausibility.js, never hand-written per-check compute. Both reuse checks[].limit's grammar under the shared name `bound`, extended with value_min/value_max (Ask 2) for a raw measured value rather than a violation count/pct/ratio. `frequency: every_run|validate_only` is the Spec 122 P3 cost-adjudication response to the 48 candidate queries measured live this WF (compute_centroids/load_ravines/link_parcel_addresses run tens of seconds to minutes per query and may not fire on every pipeline run). `when` mirrors checks[].when (pre|pre_write|post, required — Fold B-2: silent on write-ordering was a real collision risk). `source` is a required, closed self-tag (check|invariant|plausibility) carried onto the synthetic audit row so a consumer can tell DATA rows (Rule 13's own charter) from PROCESS rows without re-deriving it from array membership (Fold B-3). `last_measured` (value/at/commit/cost_ms/sample_n/source_run) is EXCLUDED from the golden fingerprint (Fold B-4) and is populated at migration time from a >=5-timings/>=2-session grounder median, never a single-session number (Fold B-1) — `sample_n` and `source_run:{run_id,chain,event}` exist because a manual run-step.mjs invocation on assert_schema/link_wsib/link_massing (3 of 6 converted steps) is ALSO a writer of this field, and the scheduled sources-chain run is ruled authoritative over it (Fold A-4e). `statement_timeout` is a per-invariant DECLARED override (required, with a stated why, whenever frequency is validate_only) — Fold B-1 struck the plan's original '110s ceiling' premise (the live server's own statement_timeout is 0/no-limit), so this is a declared value with a why, never a 'raised' override. Both categories are legally "none" once required (most steps have zero candidates until migrated); checks[] itself is untouched. STAGED, not required, at commit 1 (see x-schema-rollout, required_from_commit: 4) — an earlier draft of this text claimed commit 1 was 'no behaviour change to any existing descriptor beyond the bare stub this addition now requires every converted descriptor to declare'; that was REFUTED: adding invariants/plausibility to `required` immediately would force a bare stub onto all 6 real converted descriptors, changing their file bytes, which trips golden-fingerprint.infra.test.ts's R-C lockfile (2026-08-28, unrelated ruling) on all 6 at once — an unbudgeted live-DB recapture this commit never accounted for. Orchestrator ruling 2026-08-30 (option (c)): definitions + root properties land now, `required` flips at commit 4 once each real descriptor's own migration commit already needs a fresh capture.

x-banned-for-new.enforcer: scripts/lib/step/validate.js assertGrandfathered — ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27). Until then x-banned-for-new was METADATA WITH NO CONSUMER: nothing read it, so 'banned for new steps' was a sentence in a JSON file and any new descriptor could carry any banned value with a why. The rule is now two-part and both parts are required — a banned value needs (1) the sibling *_why the schema already demands, AND (2) an entry in the allowlist above naming the step, the exact path, the value, a why and the commit that grandfathered it. A step that is not on the list is REFUSED at pipeline.step() construction, before compute exists.

rules.was: class D (insert_only_no_retraction) as a fused identity
rules.banned_when: write_discipline.class is an insert-only mechanic AND retract == "none"
rules.why: A W3 retraction breach. Under V7 the ban is a predicate over the mechanic and the retraction axis, so a step that inserts only but DOES retract elsewhere is no longer mislabelled as breaching.

rules.was: class H (set_based_unscoped) as a fused identity
rules.banned_when: write_discipline.class is a set-based mechanic AND write_discipline.scope == "none"
rules.why: An unscoped set-based UPDATE rewrites rows it never examined. Scope is now its own declared axis, so the ban is evaluable instead of being carried inside a class name.

rules.was: not previously expressible at all — the source of GAP-1 and GAP-2
rules.why: V7 decoupling: guardedness left the class name and became the `guard` axis, so an unguarded write is now DECLARABLE (with a why) rather than unlabellable. Grandfathered only — banned for new steps.

x-mechanic-notes.V7: write_discipline.class names the write MECHANIC ONLY. Guardedness lives in `guard`, scope in `scope`, retraction in `retract`. Three of the 13 names still read as fused because the names are ported and frozen — read them as mechanics:
x-mechanic-notes.guarded_upsert: MECHANIC: keyed upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). The word 'guarded' is historical — whether it is guarded is read from `guard`, never from this name.
x-mechanic-notes.insert_only_no_retraction: MECHANIC: insert-only (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). Whether it retracts is read from `retract`; the ban is the rule no_retraction, not this name.
x-mechanic-notes.set_based_scoped: MECHANIC: set-based UPDATE. Whether it is scoped is read from `scope`, not from this name.
x-mechanic-notes.set_based_unscoped: MECHANIC: set-based UPDATE — the same mechanic as set_based_scoped. Retained as a distinct value only so existing descriptors keep their ported label; the ban is the rule unscoped_set_based, evaluated over `scope`.

x-menu-completeness.measured: 2026-08-24 (S1, ruling R5); gaps closed by operator ruling V7 the same day
x-menu-completeness.method: The 5 known evidence-base §3f mislabels were re-derived FROM THE SQL, not from the ported labels, so the 13-class enum is not authored against known-bad data.

corrections.load_heritage: A -> B. :602 is a literal `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE source_id <> ALL($1::BIGINT[])` departure delete against its own table, behind an empty-set guard (:598). The base's Del=0 is factually wrong.
corrections.load_zoning: A -> B (x11 layer tables). The departure delete at :526-528 is a NOT EXISTS anti-join against a keys-only TEMP table. The suspected class C is REFUTED: the temp table holds keys only and is never the source of an INSERT...SELECT, so it is a mechanic of B, not a full replace.
corrections.load_neighbourhoods: A -> A + 6 INEXPRESSIBLE. Confirmed: exactly 2 IS DISTINCT FROM in the whole file (:153, :154), both in the upsert. The 6 profile UPDATEs (:473, :486, :506, :543, :563, :603) have NO guard at all. Also VACUUM ANALYZE at :680 -> execution.maintenance.
corrections.link_wsib: CORRECTED (C1 MATCHER pilot, 2026-08-28) — the original 'K -> E + G' guess (below, kept for the record) was ALSO wrong, refuted by measurement: the wsib_registry write's SET clause values are per-row JOIN results from a compute-authored matched CTE, which neither class E (write_once_backfill) nor G (set_based_scoped) can generate — G's codegen writes only a DECLARED CONSTANT. The measured shape is TWO NEW mechanics: set_based_join_update (LG-11, wsib_registry link-columns + entities contact columns, both computed-from-a-join) and set_based_null_retract (LG-16, the tier-3-only retraction) + set_based_scoped (G, entities.is_wsib_registered flag, a genuine constant). There is no derived_recompute anywhere in the file; K is simply absent (this much of the original guess held). Original guess: 'K -> E + G. Three targets: wsib_registry link-columns are E (WHERE linked_entity_id IS NULL), entities.is_wsib_registered is G (guarded + scoped by match_confidence), entities contact columns are E in blank-or-null form.'
corrections.refresh_snapshot: M -> INEXPRESSIBLE. :535 is `ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE SET ... created_at=NOW()` with no change guard — a same-day re-run overwrites all columns of that day's row in place. It is not append-only.

gaps.pattern: unguarded set-based UPDATE — no IS DISTINCT FROM at all
gaps.why_inexpressible: Under the FUSED enum: G required guard AND scope; H required a guard WITHOUT scope; E required an IS NULL predicate; I required a temp table; J required multi-pass + defer; K did not cover source-loaded non-derived columns (avg/median household income, period_of_construction). Every available value would have recorded a guard the SQL does not contain.
gaps.now_expressible_as: class: set_based_scoped (MECHANIC) + guard: "none" (+guard_why) + scope: the profile-refresh predicate, or scope: "none" (+why) where the refresh genuinely spans the table.
gaps.status: EXPRESSIBLE — the per-site declaration is owed at the INGESTOR pilot's PH-0.

gaps.pattern: unguarded keyed upsert — ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE with no change guard
gaps.why_inexpressible: Under the FUSED enum: A meant GUARDED upsert; D covered DO NOTHING; M meant append-only INSERT. All three misstated an in-place same-day overwrite.
gaps.now_expressible_as: class: guarded_upsert (MECHANIC: keyed upsert) + guard: "none" (+guard_why) + scope: "snapshot_date = CURRENT_DATE".
gaps.status: EXPRESSIBLE — the declaration is owed at the RECORDER pilot's PH-0.

x-menu-completeness.root_cause: The enum FUSED the write mechanic with the change guard, so every write that lacked a guard fell off the menu.
x-menu-completeness.resolution: CLOSED BY OPERATOR RULING V7 (2026-08-24): mechanic, guard, scope and retraction are four declared axes; `guard: none` makes an unguarded write DECLARABLE (with a why) instead of unlabellable, and the D/H bans became validator rules over the axes. No enum value was invented. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: the seven sites above are expressible, not yet declared — each owning pilot must verify its own writes at PH-0 and produce the declaration. The contract is still v0 and freezes at C3.
wording_ambiguities: Class B is written as the literal `DELETE ... WHERE key <> ALL($1)`, but load-zoning expresses the identical departure delete as a NOT EXISTS anti-join. B must be read BY INTENT, not by literal syntax, or load_zoning becomes a third gap.

Classes C and I both presuppose a temp table used for full-replace / update-from; load-zoning uses one purely to scope a delete. Harmless under the per-target rule only if that rule is stated explicitly: an ON COMMIT DROP scratch table is not a write target.

x-refuted.checks[].severity: PASS is IMPOSSIBLE as a declared severity — it is a runtime outcome, never a declarable escalation target (Spec 122 §12.5). The declarable menu is INFO|WARN|FAIL.
x-refuted.identity.gate_exempt: The claim 'declaring archetype retires run-chain.js:544-550' is REFUTED — isInfraStep spans four archetypes plus name-specific exceptions. gate_exempt is the explicit field the retirement needs.
x-refuted.counters-null-for-ASSERT: 'An ASSERT emits counters: null' is REFUTED AS DESCRIPTION (0 of 5 ASSERTs do today). It is retained as a NORMATIVE requirement per §1.10's required-field profile: the descriptor must declare counters: "none".

x-schema-rollout.$comment: Staged rollout of the invariants[]/plausibility[] categories (R-T addendum, WF2 'The Step Validator, Data-First', orchestrator ruling 2026-08-30, option (c) — mirrors the converted.json PENDING staging pattern (R-K.1). RESOLVED at commit 4 (2026-08-30): both categories are now in `required`/`x-categories` (20 total) — every real descriptor already had a migrated invariants[]/plausibility[] array or an explicit 'none' (assert_schema, ASSERT archetype, 0 candidates by design) BEFORE this flip, so the required-status change itself touches zero real descriptor bytes; the byte-change->fingerprint cost rode each step's own migration commit (3 for link_massing, 4 for the other 4 + assert_schema's stub), exactly as staged. This object is kept, historical, rather than deleted — it is the record of why the staging existed and when it closed.

invariants.why: Definition + root property landed commit 1 (schema-shape only); required as of commit 4, once every real descriptor had migrated its golden invariants (link_massing commit 3; compute_centroids/link_wsib/link_parcel_addresses/load_ravines/assert_schema's 'none' stub commit 4).

plausibility.why: Same staging and resolution as invariants.

why.description: A justification WITH a liveness handle (Spec 122 §12.3, claim #239). A why that cannot be falsified when its external dependent disappears is decoration.

liveness.description: What would make this why FALSE. "none" is legal but means the why can never be retired automatically.

bound.description: R-T addendum (Ask 2) — the closed bound grammar shared by checks[].limit AND invariants[]/plausibility[].bound, one vocabulary estate-wide rather than a parallel one. value_min/value_max compare a RAW MEASURED VALUE (e.g. a row count read as a value, not a violation count) — the two forms checks[].limit's original grammar could not express (Fold A-4b: they need real verdict.js evaluateLimit branches, added at commit 2 — pop/ratio remain unevaluable in the new synthetic-check path, a pre-existing gap this WF does not close).

lastMeasured.description: R-T addendum, Fold A-1/A-4e/B-1. Populated at declaration time from a >=5-timings/>=2-distinct-session grounder median (never a single-session number — Fold B-1 struck the weaker '3x same-session' rule after measuring 2-2.6x cross-session variance on the SAME query) and EXCLUDED WHOLESALE from the golden fingerprint (Fold B-4): re-timing must never fail a fingerprint lock whose declared contract (bound/why/frequency/when/source) has not changed.

value.description: The measured value at declaration/re-measurement time, in whatever type the SQL returns.

at.description: Full ISO-8601 timestamp of the measurement (not isoDate — this needs time-of-day).

commit.description: The git commit the measurement was taken against.

cost_ms.description: The grounder median (Fold B-1), not a single sample.

sample_n.description: Fold B-1 — how many timings the median above was taken over; a single-session repeat no longer qualifies as a measurement.

source_run.description: Fold A-4e — WHICH run last stamped this field. A manual run-step.mjs invocation on a converted step (assert_schema/link_wsib/link_massing today) also restamps last_measured; the scheduled sources-chain run is ruled AUTHORITATIVE for drift/staleness reasoning, a manual restamp is operator-visibility-only.

run_id.description: pipeline_runs.id, or null for a standalone/manual measurement with no run row.

chain.description: The chain slug (e.g. "sources"), or null when not chain-spawned.

invariant.description: R-T addendum — single-table, single-step-scoped declarative-SQL data bound over THIS step's own writes. Executed generically by scripts/lib/step/plausibility.js's runInvariants; enters buildAuditTable as a SYNTHETIC selected check (Fold A-2), not merely appended to extraRows, so a BLOCKING FAIL populates errors[]/checks_failed/errorMessage exactly like a real check.

limit_from_config.description: Same rule as checks[].limit_from_config, extended verbatim (Design decisions, Tunable vs constant bullet): names a config.logic_variables[].name whose resolved value overrides `bound` at evaluation time. Absent = bound is a declared physical/structural constant and MUST carry a why explaining it (the entry-level `why` below).

when.description: Fold B-2 — mirrors checks[].when. Filters the synthetic entry through the SAME onlyChecks/gated-skip narrowing a real check gets (Fold A-3): a pre-scoped entry excluded past its write point, a post-scoped entry excluded before it.

source.description: Fold B-3 — the closed self-tag this entry's synthetic row carries, declared rather than inferred from array membership.

frequency.description: Spec 122 P3 cost-adjudication response to the 48 candidate queries measured live this WF. every_run fires at the run-end hook on every pipeline execution (budget: scripts/lib/step/plausibility.js gates it against the invariants_every_run_budget_ms logic variable, default 5000ms); validate_only fires ONLY from step:validate --write and at chain-end synthesis (Ask 6b).

statement_timeout.description: Ask 5(b) / Fold B-1 — a DECLARED per-invariant override, required whenever frequency is validate_only. Fold B-1 struck the plan's original '110s ceiling' premise (SHOW statement_timeout on the live target returns 0/no-limit, source 'default') — this is a stated value with a why, never a 'raised' override. "none" means inherit the connection's own setting.

retighten_when.description: A machine-readable STRING naming the condition that would let this bound tighten (mirrors R-H's language, e.g. "zero rows" or "population < N"). Pairs with the EXISTING <metric>_retighten companion-audit-row convention (scripts/lib/accepted-baseline.js, Spec 48 §4.9) — this is the descriptor-side declaration, the companion row is the runtime-side emission; reused, not reinvented.

plausibility.description: R-T addendum — cross-field/zone-aware declarative-SQL check that MAY span tables this step does not itself write (e.g. link_massing checking parcels.centroid_lat populated by compute_centroids). Reuse target for parsing is parcel-sanity-audit.js's ENGINE (statusFor, extracted to scripts/lib/step/plausibility.js; the verdict cascade itself is scripts/lib/step/verdict.js's deriveVerdict — Rule 10 retired the parcel-sanity-audit-local verdictCascade duplicate), never its CHECKS[] entries — those are spliced into one folded query with no per-check id, so a plausibility[] entry structurally cannot reference one 1:1 and carries its own standalone SQL (Fold A-4d: duplication of predicate text is accepted this WF, filed as a nice_to_have for a future per-check-id pass).

limit_from_config.description: Same rule as checks[].limit_from_config, extended verbatim.

source.description: Fold B-3 — the closed self-tag this entry's synthetic row carries.

zone_by.description: Optional zone-aware scoping (e.g. a zoning classification column), mirroring parcel-sanity-audit.js's own zone-scoped CHECKS[] entries (10 of 42, Fold B-7 recount). "none" (the default reading when absent) means the bound applies estate-wide.

kind.description: Fold B-7 — "distribution" reuses parcel-sanity-audit.js's separate 8-entry DIST_FIELDS percentile/outlier scan (INFO-only, no pass/fail verdict) via a direct function call, never a duplicated implementation. Absent means the ordinary bound-checked row type.

vocabulary.description: Spec 122 §12.3 — a frozen VALUE domain for a column. emits declares keys; nothing declared values, which is why ADDRESS_STATUS read 'None' for 525,346 of 525,346 rows and passed.

writeDiscipline.description: Spec 122 §1.4 — PER WRITE TARGET, never per step. The class SELECTS THE GENERATED SQL; a hand-written INSERT ... ON CONFLICT in a compute fails lint.

class.description: V7 (2026-08-24): the write MECHANIC ONLY. The 13 MEASURED classes stand as mechanics; guardedness moved out to `guard`, scope to `scope`, retraction to `retract`. Three names still READ as fused (guarded_upsert, insert_only_no_retraction, set_based_scoped/unscoped) because the ported labels are frozen — see x-mechanic-notes; never infer a guard or a scope from a class name. Re-derived per step at PH-0: the ported labels are wrong for 5 steps.
class.x-class-letters-note: N and O are LG-11/LG-16 (pilot 4, C1 MATCHER, 2026-08-28). N is a scoped UPDATE ... FROM (<compute-authored matched CTE>) with INSERT structurally forbidden — write.js's executeSetBasedJoinUpdate refuses any SQL text containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT at execution time, not merely by convention. O is the UPDATE-to-NULL retraction shape for a target this step does not OWN (wsib_registry rows are load-wsib.js's exclusive territory) — codegen-identical to set_based_scoped/unscoped (a constant SET over a declared scope, via columns[].set_value: null) but declared under its own class so a retract_when: full_only null-retraction reads as a DISTINCT mechanic from a plain flag clear, per LG-16's fence lock (never DELETE).

guard.description: V7 — THE GUARD AXIS, decoupled from the mechanic. This field alone says whether the write is change-guarded; a class name never does. `none` is DECLARABLE (it is what makes GAP-1's six unguarded UPDATEs and GAP-2's unguarded keyed upsert expressible at all) but requires a why and is grandfathered — banned for new steps.

scope.description: V7 — THE SCOPE AXIS, decoupled from the mechanic. The predicate narrowing WHICH ROWS this target writes, beyond matching the key. `none` means the write touches the whole table; combined with a set-based mechanic that is the banned unscoped_set_based configuration. A key-equality join is NOT a scope.

guard_columns_why.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull) — the LG-9 escape hatch, and the ONLY way a columns[].source "run_at" column may sit in the change guard. scripts/lib/step/validate.js refuses that combination outright without this why, because it is not a style preference: a run-clock column is DISTINCT FROM its stored value on every run, so guarding on it turns a no-op re-run into a full re-stamp of the table and re-scopes every downstream consumer keyed on that watermark.

declared_drift.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). WHAT drifts, for a target whose idempotent_rerun is declared_drift. idempotent_rerun_why says WHY zero_writes is unachievable; this says WHICH rows move and how many, so a differential can tell the DECLARED drift apart from a regression. link_massing's E1 is the worked example: the is_primary = false clear always rewrites the batch's primaries before the upsert restores them (fence 5bb31faf / B-8), so its row count is a function of the batch, not of the data changing.

expected_change_ratio.description: Measured every run from rows_scanned / rows_changed and CHECKED against this bound.

idempotent_rerun.description: zero_writes is ASSERTED, not asserted-to: run twice, the second run updates 0 (founding commit 7e130bff, lessons.md:28).

set_source.description: LG-22 (BACKFILL pilot 6 follow-on WF3, CC-D3, 2026-08-30) — OPTIONAL, applies ONLY to a set-based mechanic (set_based_scoped/set_based_unscoped/set_based_null_retract). ABSENT (the default, every pre-existing set-based target) means the SET clause is `columns[].set_value`, a DECLARED CONSTANT rendered through write.js's sqlLiteral, which structurally refuses anything but boolean/number/null — the generated statement binds no row values at all. `"compute"` means the SET clause's right-hand sides are SERVER-SIDE EXPRESSIONS over the row itself (e.g. compute_centroids's FULL-mode repair: `ST_Y(ST_Centroid(geom))`, not a literal) — buildWritePlan returns a DESCRIPTIVE plan only (mirrors set_based_join_update/insert_only_no_retraction/write_once_backfill's own `generated_by: "compute"` split) and the compute authors the real statement text, executed by write.js's executeGuardedUpdate. Widening sqlLiteral itself to accept a raw SQL fragment was rejected as an injection surface for every OTHER set-based target; this field opts a target OUT of codegen only when the descriptor says so explicitly.

allOf.x-rule: full_replace must be declared, never silent (load-centreline's staging replace is spec-sanctioned, Spec 62 L26).
V7 ban unscoped_set_based, evaluated over the decoupled axes rather than a fused class identity. An existing unscoped set-based write must still say why.

sourceKeyPolicy.description: R6 ruling — a per-target field, not a category. load-massing.js:239-247: 'Identical geometries produce duplicate hashes ... Last write wins.'

columns.description: OBJECT form only. The string-array form shown illustratively in Spec 122 §1.4 cannot carry §12.3's vocabulary field; the schema is canonical (R2).

written.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). Does the STEP supply this column's value, or does the DATABASE? `PIPELINE_META.writes` has always listed every column of the target — including `created_at`, which the step never writes and the DDL defaults — so the declaration and the generated INSERT column list are NOT the same list. Stating it is what lets the generator emit the right INSERT while `deriveMeta` keeps emitting the full declared set, instead of one of the two being quietly wrong. Default: "step".

bind.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). How the generated statement binds this column's parameter. "value" is a plain `$n`; "wkb_geometry" wraps it as `ST_GeomFromWKB($n, <guards.srid>)`, which is the only reason a class-B generator would need to know a column is spatial. Default: "value".

source.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). WHERE this column's value comes from. "compute" is the default and means the step's own row builder supplied it. "run_at" means the value IS the run clock (pipeline.getDbTimestamp, Spec 47 R3.5), and declaring it is what makes the D-5 trap MECHANICALLY unreachable: a run-clock column is DISTINCT FROM its stored value on EVERY run, so putting it in write_discipline.guard_columns — directly, or by expanding all_declared over it — rewrites every row of the table every run. scripts/lib/step/validate.js refuses that combination unless guard_columns_why is present (LG-9). Measured blast radius on parcel_buildings: 520,492 rows rewritten per run, re-scoping enrich_parcels from 1,395 parcels to 485,135.

set_value.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). The CONSTANT this column is set to by a set-based mechanic, whose generated statement is UPDATE <table> SET <col> = <set_value> WHERE <write_discipline.scope> and which therefore binds no row values at all. Only a set-based target needs it; a keyed upsert reads its values from the row builder. Declaring the constant is what keeps the generator domain-free — the alternative is a false literal inside scripts/lib/step/write.js, i.e. exactly the step-specific runner path Gate 0 (claim #149) bans.

key_sql_type.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). The SQL type the scoped departure DELETE casts its key array to (`<key> <> ALL($1::<type>[])`). Only a `retract: "departed"` target needs it, and getting it wrong is a runtime cast error rather than a silent mis-retraction. Default: "BIGINT".

retract_when.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). WHEN the declared retract actually fires. The retract enum is x-frozen, so the qualifier is a SIBLING rather than a fourth enum value. "always" is the default and the pre-existing behaviour (a class-B departure DELETE runs every load). "full_only" means the retraction is issued ONLY when staleness.mode_select resolved to full mode — which is fence b16c036's whole shape: link_massing's mass DELETE of every link for centroid-bearing parcels is correct in a FULL relink and catastrophic in an incremental one, where it would retract 520,492 rows and rebuild only the 1,395-parcel unmatchable tail. Before this field that gate was an if (FULL_MODE) in a hand-written step and nothing declared it.

allOf.x-rule: V7 ban no_retraction, evaluated over the mechanic AND the retraction axis (which are siblings here, not inside write_discipline). An insert-only mechanic that DOES retract is no longer mislabelled as a W3 breach; one that does not must say why.

limit_from_config.description: OPERATOR RULING A-4 (2026-08-25, INGESTOR pilot) — the P1↔P4 resolution. A verdict bound that is ALSO an operator knob names its `config.logic_variables[].name` here; scripts/lib/step/verdict.js substitutes the RESOLVED value into `limit` before evaluating, so the audit row's `threshold` column renders THE VALUE IN FORCE, not a stale literal, at zero extra bytes (the value is already stamped in records_meta.config). DECISION, documented rather than left ambiguous: `limit` STAYS REQUIRED and keeps its numeric form — it carries the SEED DEFAULT, so a descriptor read on its own still states a bound, and `limit_from_config` is the runtime override. The named variable MUST be declared in this descriptor's `config.logic_variables[]`; a name bound to no declaration, or bound to more than one check, is a validator-side finding.

kind.description: 9 named types (Spec 122 §12.5 corrects the '12', which was Spec 120 §5.0's list of GENERATORS) + plan_shape, ruled in by R6 as a check kind rather than a category.

expect.description: OPEN — domain knowledge. No vocabulary could supply that WARD is text in the CoA Active resource and WARD_NUMBER is int4 in Closed.

severity.description: Orthogonal to blocking. PASS is NOT declarable (§12.5) — it is a runtime outcome.

blocking.description: Orthogonal to severity: FAIL severity + blocking:false is 'report loudly, do not halt'.

when.description: The LIFECYCLE POSITION at which the runner scores this check. `pre` = before acquisition (scored even on a gated skip). `pre_write` = after acquisition + read-only validation and BEFORE any write statement (OPERATOR RULING, Fold C 2026-08-26): a FAIL row here with no active `override.accept_anomaly` entry SKIPS the write entirely — no transaction is opened — which is how Spec 59 L7/L8's "abort BEFORE any DB write" guarantee survives the archetype's acquire-then-check phase order. `post` = after the write, over `ctx.written`. A `pre_write` check must be computable from `ctx.acquired`/`ctx.prior` alone; reading `ctx.written` there is a validator-side finding.

chains.description: Per-chain check selection. assert_schema is shared x3: permits validates permit columns, sources validates source archives, parcels is validated by all three.

accept_until.description: Spec 122 §12.3 — baseline acceptance and threshold EXPIRY. Claim #228 already assumes this field exists.

retighten_when.description: R-T addendum, commit 3 (R-H, 2026-08-28 — 'carried to pilot 4', unmet until now). A machine-readable STRING naming the condition that would let this check's severity tighten (e.g. "zero rows" or "population < N") — the SAME field/grammar `invariants[]`/`plausibility[]` carry (Design decisions), extended to `checks[]` because R-H's own dispositioned checks (LM-D6/LM-D11) are pre-existing `checks[]` entries, not new declared invariants. Pairs with the EXISTING <metric>_retighten companion-audit-row convention (scripts/lib/accepted-baseline.js, Spec 48 §4.9) — this is the descriptor-side declaration, the companion row is the runtime-side emission, reused not reinvented. Optional: only a WARN-severity check with a standing non-zero population carries one.

kind.description: fk (added at the LINK pilot, 2026-08-27): a named FOREIGN KEY constraint, probed via pg_constraint contype = f. A junction table is only meaningful while BOTH sides stay referential, and a dropped FK is invisible to an index probe — a full-mode retraction would simply leave orphans for a later chain step to report. rls_bypass_or_policy (added at the INGESTOR pilot, 2026-08-25): the named table has RLS ENABLED, so the write path is only reachable when the pipeline role either bypasses RLS (pg_roles.rolbypassrls) or a policy grants it. Measured on `ravines`: relrowsecurity=true with ZERO policies — a non-bypass role UPSERTs and DELETEs 0 rows with NO error, so the write counters read 0 and the verdict reads PASS. That is indistinguishable from an unchanged source, which is why the precondition is checked BEFORE the write and fails loud.

on_missing.description: R6 ruling. 6 steps use a missing extension as an ALGORITHM SELECTOR, not a failure — which makes outputs.columns a fiction on the degraded branch.

algorithm.description: Required when on_missing=degrade: which algorithm the degraded branch uses.

match.description: A selector over the drifting layer/resource, or the literal "default".

source.description: Which compute variable feeds this counter. Retires the 9 distinct semantics measured for records_total.

scoped_by.description: The outputs.writes[].key this counter counts, or "step" for a whole-step count. §11 counter scoping.

status.description: Spec 120 §3.2b run-status vocabulary, minus 'running' which is not terminal.

records_meta.description: The records_meta SHAPE this exit path emits. NOTE: no verdict key is permitted anywhere in a terminal — the verdict is runner-owned and row-derived, which is exactly what retires the 7 hardcoded skip-path 'PASS'es.

display_name.description: The human-readable name emitted in records_meta.audit_table.name.

lock.description: V2: unique across manifest UNION one-time/ UNION backfill/ (the wider universe). Cross-file uniqueness is enforced by the validator, not by this schema.

why_lock.description: Required in substance iff lock != spec number; "none" must still be written. The lock-vs-spec comparison is validator-side.

archetype.description: V1: FULL WORDS. Drives the required-field profile (§1.10) — this field is load-bearing, not a label.

gate_exempt.description: Explicit replacement for run-chain.js:544-550's NAME-PREFIX dispatch. isInfraStep spans four archetypes plus name-specific exceptions, so archetype alone cannot derive it (§12.5).

externals.description: R6: the acquisition category folds in HERE plus staleness.trigger[].position. Four loaders use fs.existsSync as their ENTIRE freshness policy — a 9th, undeclared gate that defeats staleness.trigger. load-massing.js:28-36 records the 86-minute production failure it caused.

license.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). The publisher's licence URL. It was a module constant read by exactly one audit row (`dataset_source_license`); as descriptor data the acquisition seam can hand it to the compute on the SKIP path too, where no download happened and no constant would have been reachable.

key_property.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). For a record-bearing external (shapefile .dbf, CSV, GeoJSON properties): the SOURCE-SIDE attribute that becomes `outputs.writes[].key`. Declaring it is what lets a generic parser run without knowing the domain — and it makes an upstream rename (the #426 class) a descriptor diff instead of an undeclared constant inside a loader.

cache.description: The acquisition policy. reuse_if_present IS the existsSync class — declaring it makes the fiction visible and forces a why.

writes.description: ORDER IS DECLARED and the runner executes it in order — 'retract then rebuild' stops being a prose convention.

cascades.description: A target this step does not OWN is a cascade, never a write. load-massing.js:208,222 DELETEs from parcel_buildings (step 15's table) while emitMeta declares only building_footprints — the undeclared-telemetry class (orphan #234).

invalidates.description: list of {table, column, when} — the declared invalidator. An ENRICHER whose staleness.scope is a lineage predicate CANNOT omit it (claim #54); a write_once_backfill class-E target cannot either (§5.4a).

write_inventory.description: Spec 122 §12.3 claim #236 — the RUNTIME write-statement count must equal the declared one.

staleness.description: V5 — RESHAPED into three axes. The scalar `pending` conflated which-rows, whether-to-act and in-which-mode, and could express none of the run-ledger gate's 4 arms, the two-tier pre/post-download split, decideCentrelineMode's tri-state, or scope-defer.

scope.description: WHICH ROWS are eligible: an SQL predicate, all, or none.

trigger.description: What makes the step ELIGIBLE TO ACT. A SET, ordered by lifecycle position — two-tier metadata->hash is two gates at two positions.

signal.x-config-version-note: ADDED AT THE MATCHER PILOT (2026-08-28, LG-12/A-3). An operator-edited logic_variables row with NO pipeline_runs producer of its own (link_wsib's wsib_fuzzy_match_threshold — readThresholdVersionSignal/hasThresholdChanged, generalized). Pairs with `variable` below.

position.description: R6: the ACQUISITION LIFECYCLE POSITION. pre_acquisition = HEAD/ETag before download; acquisition = the existsSync short-circuit; post_acquisition = content hash after download; pre_compute = ledger/code/interval gates.

external.description: The inputs.reads.externals[].id this trigger reads, where applicable.

table.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). The table an upstream_ledger signal COUNTS. Without it the runner cannot evaluate a data-side gate generically and the comparison has to live in a step-specific helper — which is what scripts/lib/massing-full-gate.js is, and why Gate 0 (claim #149) would fire if the library named it.

emit_key.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull). The emits[].key in the PRIOR completed run's records_meta this signal compares THIS run's measurement against. code_version compares staleness.logic_version; upstream_ledger compares COUNT(*) over table; config_version compares the named variable's logic_variables.updated_at. Naming the key in the descriptor is what lets ONE generic reader serve every code+data gate — and it is the same key the frozen producer contract already publishes, so the gate and the emit can never drift apart.

variable.description: ADDED AT THE MATCHER PILOT (2026-08-28, LG-12/A-3). The logic_variables.variable_key a config_version signal reads updated_at for. Required when signal is config_version.

mode_select.description: What the trigger CHOOSES. The massing code+data veto outputs a MODE, not a skip; scope-defer is the inverse of a staleness gate (too much changed, so refuse).

fingerprint.description: ALWAYS ON, never declared. Normalized hash over compute + outputs/staleness/guards/execution + the ENUMERATED external inputs below. Never over identity/why/notes/deviations.

fingerprint_inputs.description: NEW (§1.5). Closes the contradiction that §4.1a rules an unenumerated external input a declaration defect while fingerprint is marked derived-do-not-declare. LINK_MASSING_CODE_VERSION lives in scripts/lib/, not in the step, and triggers a full destructive rebuild (claim #52b).

on_prior_run_error.description: §1.6 — the DECLARED posture when the PRIOR-RUN read that feeds every trigger fails (LR-D2, peel 8a). The prior run's emit block is the baseline both gate tiers and every drift ratio compare against, so a failed read is not a neutral event: it silently downgrades the step to "first run", which loads unguarded with every ratio 0 BY DEFINITION rather than by measurement. fail_step = the read is load-bearing, refuse. warn_row = proceed with no baseline and say so in a `prior_run_read_failed` audit row — never silently, which is what the pre-conversion `.catch(warn => null)` did. ABSENT means fail_step: the posture may be unstated, but it may not be silent.

schema_drift.description: V3: none|propagate|pause ('warn' dropped — a drift response is an ACTION). R6: a scalar OR a CONDITIONAL PER-LAYER ARRAY, because load-zoning.js:405-407 responds differently per layer in ONE step (base FAIL/pause, non-base WARN/propagate). The array must carry a "default" arm; the exactly-one-default rule is validator-side.

shape.description: ADDED AT THE LINK PILOT (2026-08-27, C3 pre-pull) — OPERATOR RULING A-1(a). WHICH lifecycle the runner drives, DECLARED rather than sniffed. Until this field the branch was inferred: scripts/lib/step/index.js isIngestStep required an inputs.reads.externals[].url, so a pure DB-to-DB join (a LINK) silently fell to the ASSERT path and its join and write had NO HOME AT ALL. Inference is the wrong mechanism for a phase order that carries before/after guarantees (B-1..B-13): a step whose declaration says nothing gets whichever branch a predicate happens to pick. "assert" = compute only, the runner writes nothing. "ingest" = acquire, validate, pre_write gate, write (runIngestPhase). "link" = read, staleness/mode, RUN_AT, pre_write gate, ordered writes[], post checks (runLinkPhase). "cascade" = ADDED AT THE MATCHER PILOT (2026-08-28, A-1 SHOULD-FIX d) — a bulk N-tier cascade over a declared `tiers[]` array with NO batching/pagination and MORE THAN ONE write target per tier (runCascadePhase): read, gated-skip, staleness/mode, RUN_AT, pre_write gate, ordered per-tier writes[] inside ONE step-scoped transaction, post checks. Measured at commit 7 to fork `runLinkPhase`'s keyset batch loop and its flat parcels_* counters rather than fit a `tiers[]` branch inside it — link_wsib is the first and, as of this pilot, only cascade-shaped step. "materialize" = ADDED AT THE MATERIALIZER PILOT (2026-08-29, A-1 RULING) — ONE unconditional bulk INSERT...SELECT...JOIN <spatial predicate>...ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING statement, no retraction, no primary/fallback split, no tiers (runMaterializePhase): guards.requires, LG-15 ledger gated-skip, RUN_AT, the keyset-paginated per-batch transaction loop calling LG-18's executeInsertSelectNoRetract, post checks. Forked from runCascadePhase's phase-order shape (guards -> gated-skip -> RUN_AT -> pre_write gate -> write -> post checks), NOT an extension of runLinkPhase: runLinkPhase's write path is SELECT-then-batched-executeUpsertBatch, which would split this archetype's single server-side statement and break the G2 "verbatim SQL" guarantee. link_parcel_addresses is the first and, as of this pilot, only materialize-shaped step. "backfill" = ADDED AT THE BACKFILL PILOT (2026-08-29, A-4 RULING, ACCEPT at Fold D) — ONE conditional set-based UPDATE...WHERE <scope> statement, UPDATE-only (LG-20's executeBackfillUpdate), no retraction, no batching in the surviving (PostGIS-only) path, no ledger-gated skip (runBackfillPhase): guards.requires, a pre-run backlog count, a DATA-driven (not staleness-gated) zero-work completion when the backlog is 0, RLS preflight, pre_write gate, the one statement, post checks. Forked from runMaterializePhase's phase-order shape, NOT an extension of it: a MATERIALIZER's write is a keyset-paginated batch loop over MANY statements; a BACKFILL's ONE write target is a SINGLE unpaginated statement with `txn_scope: "statement"` and no batch loop at all. compute_centroids is the first and, as of this pilot, only backfill-shaped step. "link_keyed" = ADDED AT PILOT 7 (2026-08-30, LINK pilot 7, `link_parcels`, Fold B item 4) — FORKED FROM `runLinkPhase` UNCONDITIONALLY (the pilot-4 fork precedent, `index.js:263-268`, was never itself gated on a line-count threshold), NOT a branch inside it: `runLinkPhase`'s single-integer `id` keyset (`eligible_batch_sql` + a `lastId` cursor) cannot page a table whose PK is a composite `(permit_num, revision_num)` with no surrogate `id` (LG-25's own composite-key keyset, `(permit_num, revision_num) > ($2, $3)`); its ONE primary + ONE fallback match pass cannot express a 4-tier cascade (address UNION ALL primary, spatial containment, spatial KNN fallback); and its class-B-shaped single write target cannot express class F's compound upsert-then-keyed-DELETE (LG-24's `executeGuardedDeleteByKey`, run inside the SAME batch transaction as the upsert, Fold B item 5's declared `writes[]` order). `runLinkPhase` (245 lines) is left byte-for-byte untouched — `link_massing` keeps using it exactly as before. `link_parcels` is the first and, as of this pilot, only link_keyed-shaped step. "recorder" = ADDED AT PILOT 8 (2026-08-31, RECORDER pilot 8, `refresh_snapshot`, Fold B — zero-growth hypothesis REFUTED by direct trace against all six existing runners) — the SIMPLEST runner in the library (`runRecorderPhase`): no batching, no carried-rows loop, no ledger gate — compute produces exactly ONE row, one single-statement `guarded_upsert` write (`executeRecorderUpsert`, a new write.js executor) in ONE transaction. Mode/staleness derivation, `chain_run_id` (R-U), `records_meta`, and the verdict cascade all reuse the existing generic paths unchanged — this shape adds NO new mechanism beyond the runner + executor pair. Forked from `runBackfillPhase`'s phase-order shape (guards -> pre-write gate -> the one statement -> post checks, no gated-skip) — NOT an extension of it: `executeBackfillUpdate` structurally refuses any INSERT token (UPDATE-only, LG-20), and a RECORDER's write IS an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE`, which `write_once_backfill`'s own class contract cannot express. Measured against all six prior shapes before adding this one (`ingest`/`link`/`link_keyed`/`cascade`/`materialize` all require either an acquisition seam, a join/carried-rows batch loop, or a ledger gate none of which this step has; `backfill`'s executor is UPDATE-only by construction) — none fit. `refresh_snapshot` is the first and, as of this pilot, only recorder-shaped step. ABSENT keeps the pre-existing inference exactly, so no converted step changes behaviour.

tiers.description: ADDED AT THE MATCHER PILOT (2026-08-28, A-1). Required when shape is "cascade": the ORDERED N-tier match cascade, highest confidence first — a higher tier's write scope (`WHERE linked_entity_id IS NULL`-shaped) must exclude any row a prior tier already claimed, which is what makes each tier's counters and writes independent of loop order. Each tier names the confidence variable its writes stamp; the compute's buildTierSql(descriptor, config, tier, mode) is the ONLY place the tier's match predicate and write SQL are authored (Rule 2 — compute is domain logic only).

confidence_from_config.description: The config.logic_variables[].name whose resolved value this tier stamps as the write's confidence column. Named with the *_from_config suffix (§1.2a P4) so the generic conformance battery's fromConfigRefs scan counts this as a genuine consumption path — a bare `confidence_config` name does not match that suffix and reads as a dead declaration the moment the compute reaches it only by indirection (LW-D10's blind spot).

max_iterations_from_config.description: OPTIONAL. Present ONLY on a tier whose mode-"full" pass must loop to convergence rather than run once (LG-16/T7, LW-D10) — names the config.logic_variables[].name bounding the iteration count. Its PRESENCE is what the runner (runCascadePhase) uses to decide which tier(s) loop in mode full; absence means the tier always runs its single-pass write, in every mode. Declared, never inferred from a tier id string (Gate 0 — the library carries no link_wsib-specific branch).

batch_size_from_config.description: OPTIONAL, MATERIALIZER pilot (2026-08-29, LW-D10 class). `execution.batch` (above) is frozen to a literal integer or "none" — it cannot express a config-driven batch size. Present ONLY on a step whose keyset-paginated batch loop reads its per-batch row count from `config.logic_variables[].name` rather than a hardcoded literal: names that logic variable, with the *_from_config suffix (§1.2a P4) so the generic conformance battery's fromConfigRefs scan counts this as a genuine consumption path — mirroring `tiers[].confidence_from_config`/`max_iterations_from_config`'s own precedent for the identical blind spot (a runner-resolved value the compute never spells `ctx.config.<name>` for).

partial_fill.description: The 5 measured classes (§3g). Only ONE step has a real recovery ledger; for the other twelve batched steps nothing in the database can answer 'is this table half-loaded?'.

on_batch_error.description: NEW (§1.6). A WHOLE BATCH swallowed and discarded, counted as one row error — load-address-points.js:374-378, load-parcels.js:550-554, load-massing.js:378-382.

on_check_error.description: NEW (§1.6). The CHECK QUERY ITSELF errors — today the row is silently omitted, so a dropped table is indistinguishable from a healthy one (assert-data-bounds.js:607-610, assert-schema.js:445-449).

on_degrade.description: NEW (§1.6) and the one that matters. 'On failure, substitute prior-run values or zeroes and present them as current' — live in four places in refresh-snapshot.js behind a hardcoded PASS. Declaring it does not make it acceptable; it makes it visible, and +why makes it adjudicated.

timeout_from_config.description: Ruling A-4, generalized past `checks[].limit_from_config` (peel 8c). A timeout is simultaneously DESCRIPTOR DATA (P1.1 — a reader must see a bound without a database) and an OPERATOR KNOB (P4 — a hard-coded knob is a hidden variable). Declaring both as literals is two sources of truth that drift silently. So `timeout` carries the SEED DEFAULT and this names the logic variable whose RESOLVED value the runner uses instead: ONE source, descriptor-derives-from-config, with the literal as the stated fallback for a database that has not been seeded. The step's own conformance lock asserts the two AGREE.

redact.description: Spec 122 §12.3 claim #276 — values that MUST be scrubbed before persistence. Nowhere else in the contract can say this.

invocation.description: PER CHAIN argv/env, so manifest<->descriptor drift is a CHECKABLE difference rather than a convention. The manifest chain_args --full pin that killed enrich_parcels' incremental path is exactly this class (concern 15).

maintenance.description: R6: NOT a category — a field. VACUUM ANALYZE on 4 tables across 3 steps; it CONSTRAINS txn_scope (VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction) and targets tables the issuing step does not own, while an ASSERT does it with outputs forced to "none".

then.description: A step-scoped transaction cannot contain a VACUUM.

checks.description: THE ONE CATEGORY THAT MAY NEVER BE "none" (claim #7). pipeline.step() validates the descriptor BEFORE compute runs, so a step cannot execute without declaring checks.

invariants.description: R-T addendum (Spec 124 §2 Rule 13, 2026-08-29) — single-table, single-step-scoped declarative-SQL data bounds over THIS step's own writes. "none" is legal and is every converted step's state until its own migration commit populates it (Spec 124 §9: assert_schema has 0 candidates by design — ASSERT writes nothing).

plausibility.description: R-T addendum — cross-field/zone-aware declarative-SQL checks that may span tables this step does not itself write. "none" is legal.

override.description: The force env vars. 6 *_FORCE_FULL hatches exist today, all ad hoc — this makes the name a declared field instead of an invention.

dry_run.description: MOST steps' dry-run is env-var-driven; link_wsib's is ARGV-driven (`process.argv.includes('--dry-run')`, G-5) — declaring the literal flag is what lets `staleness.dryRunArgPresent` be the one place it is read (ADDED AT THE MATCHER PILOT, 2026-08-28).

accept_anomaly.description: OPERATOR RULING A-5 (2026-08-25, INGESTOR pilot) — THE FOURTH KIND OF OVERRIDE. force_full / force_run / dry_run all answer "does the step act?"; an accept-anomaly answers "the step acted, a declared check FAILED, proceed anyway". Present in >=2 loaders today as ad-hoc env reads (RAVINE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT, RAVINE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE). Declaring it makes the L7c rule STRUCTURAL rather than textual: the override lets the run COMPLETE, it NEVER suppresses the FAIL row. `check_id` must name a declared check; the runner also emits a WARN row whenever the env is standing, so an accidental prod override is visible even on a run it never had to rescue.

emits.description: Additional records_meta keys BEYOND runner defaults. Q1 warns 13 top-level keys are already taken.

skeleton.description: ADDED AT THE INGESTOR PILOT (2026-08-25). The FIELD SET and default values of an `object`-typed emit — the frozen producer block a consumer reads (Spec 59 §9's 18-field records_meta.ravine_load). Two runner behaviours need it and neither can be derived from `type: "object"`: (1) a GATED SKIP re-emits the prior run's block through sourceVersion.buildSkipReEmitMeta(skeleton <- prior <- pins), and a skeleton typed only as "object" gives the merge no keys; (2) a FAILURE terminal emits the skeleton with whatever is known so far. Declaring it here is P1.1 (descriptor data before code): the 7 fields the consumer HALTs on become greppable in the descriptor instead of living in a hand-written literal inside the step.

interpretation.description: Prose lives in <slug>.notes.json, capped at 12 entries. Checks are uncapped; prose is capped — the cheapest way to keep knowledge is to make it measurable. May reference a check id but may NEVER quote a number.

interrupted.description: OPERATOR RULING R-B (2026-08-28, ADVERSARY DELTA — measured 2026-08-28: link_massing forced FULL killed mid-rebuild left parcel_buildings at 29,330/520,492 rows; the next run's gate read "unchanged" and went incremental, so the hole persisted). WHAT the step's recovery posture is when a process is killed mid-write. `force_full_on_next_run` is the truthful posture until the library implements the marker-based reader (deferred to pilot 4, declared gap filed in docs/reports/review_followups.md — a crashed/stuck-running row newer than the last completed run must read as a FULL signal). `none` is legal only with `interrupted_why` and is a WARN in conformance — every `outputs.writes[]` entry with `retract_when: full_only` or `retract: "all"` REQUIRES `interrupted: "force_full_on_next_run"` (step-conformance.infra.test.ts), because a crashed retraction on that target leaves a hole no incremental run's staleness gate can see.

before_image.description: OPERATOR RULING R-M (2026-08-28, LG-17). Any write target that RETRACTS (write_discipline.class "set_based_null_retract", or retract "all"/"departed") writes the rows it is about to retract (key columns + the columns it nulls/deletes) to a dated JSONL file (docs/reports/golden/<slug>/before-image/<RUN_AT ISO>-<target>.jsonl) INSIDE the same run, BEFORE the retraction statement — a destructive repair with no row-level before-image cannot be audited. `"generated"` means the runner writes this file automatically (scripts/lib/step/write.js writeBeforeImage, called from the runner before executeSetBasedClear/executeRetraction); on a write failure the run FAILS before retracting (fail loud, never a silent skip). `"none"` is legal only with `before_image_why` and is a WARN in conformance — every destructive-retraction target REQUIRES `before_image: "generated"` (step-conformance.infra.test.ts), same enforcement shape as `interrupted` above.

database.description: Retires the defect class where 4 analysis scripts defaulted to the PRE-CUTOVER database: same audit, same commit, 2,394 violations / 0 FAIL gates versus 30,288 / 1. A step pointed at a 222-migration database REFUSES.

min_migration.description: COUNT floor, not a filename number: the step refuses to run unless COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations is >= this value (scripts/lib/resolve-db.js assertDbTarget, operator ruling P0 9e2da7b1). The migrations/ filename sequence has historical gaps (e.g. 43, 49, 50, 158), so a required migration's FILENAME number is always >= its true COUNT position once gaps exist — setting min_migration to the filename (LW-D8: 243 instead of 240 for migration 243_wsib_unlinked_partial_index.sql) makes the floor unreachable forever. Set this to the 1-based position of the required migration file in the sorted migrations/ directory listing.

counters.description: Which variable feeds records_total / _new / _updated. Retires 9 distinct measured semantics for records_total (3 scripts emit 1 for 'one audit pass', 2 emit 0 for the same thing) and >=13 counter-scoping incidents.

config.description: 5 of 12 steps calling loadMarketplaceConfigs declare NO schema. 400 logic-variable entries carry 798 bounds with ZERO bound-readers.

hoisted_above_gate.description: link-wsib's A1/A2 fence: a SKIP-eligible step must never let an invalid threshold hide behind a green SKIPPED summary, so config validation runs ABOVE the lock and the gate.

retired.description: OPERATOR RULING R-A (2026-08-28). Retirement of a tunable is itself a declaration, never a live registry row: an operator-editable knob with zero effect is a FALSE AFFORDANCE. `retired ∩ logic_variables` MUST be empty (step-conformance.infra.test.ts) — a name lives in exactly one of the two arrays, never both. A retired name must appear in NO seed (scripts/seeds/logic_variables.json), NO GlobalConfigCard GROUPS entry and NO ctx.config read in the compute (same conformance suite). `scripts/lib/step/config.js resolveConfig` widens its declared-names presence SELECT to declared ∪ retired and stamps a `retired_var_row_present` audit row (WARN when the row still exists, INFO once an operator has deleted it) until the row is gone — ADVERSARY DELTA R-A.

probe_presence.description: OPERATOR RULING R-D (2026-08-28). Cloud parity is a chain-start assertion: a name here is NOT this step's own tunable (that is `logic_variables[]`) and is never projected into `ctx.config` — it is a FLEET-WIDE name (typically another converted step's declared logic variable) this step ONLY probes for a `logic_variables` ROW, so a chain-start step like `assert_schema` can FAIL at minute zero, naming the remedy, instead of a downstream step throwing LM-D15's mid-chain error however many steps later it happens to sit. `scripts/lib/step/config.js resolveConfig` widens its EXISTING declared ∪ retired presence SELECT to declared ∪ retired ∪ probe (the SAME query, no new path — the mechanism R-A already established) and the runner hands the measured `{name, present}[]` to the compute as `ctx.probePresence`, never as a value — a probed name is observed, never consumed. Optional array, default `[]`.

sharing.description: The SECOND classification axis. Archetype answers what kind of step this is; sharing answers how many chains it must be correct in AT ONCE — 14 shared steps across 36 slots estate-wide, 10 across 28 touching sources.

chains.description: From manifest.chains. NEVER declared, or it drifts — link-wsib.js:55 hand-maintains four spellings, one of them refuted in-file.

phase.description: An EXPLICIT MAP, never a ternary. link_parcels computes chainId === 'sources' ? 6 : 9 at :186 and PIPELINE_CHAIN === 'sources' ? 6 : 7 at :660 — the same axis, in one file, disagreeing on the non-sources value. A map cannot disagree with itself.

on_contention.description: self_skip is today's default, not a decision anyone made. Contention IS already observable (pipeline.js:906/:932) — the field survives on the narrower premise that two chains can run concurrently.

terminals.description: R6 — THE 18TH CATEGORY. 10 exit paths in one step, each with a hand-written records_meta: the source of the 7 hardcoded skip-path 'PASS'es this contract exists to retire. No terminal may declare a verdict; the verdict is runner-owned and row-derived.

allOf.x-profile: ASSERT — 3 categories collapse to "none" (§1.10). counters is normative here, not descriptive: 0 of 5 ASSERTs comply today.

INGESTOR — write_discipline + retract + replay + empty_source all required (write_discipline/retract/replay are required on every write globally; what the profile adds is that outputs may not be "none").
LINK / MATCHER — invalidates required (non-empty) and counters scoped by writes.key.
ENRICHER — claim #54: a staleness.scope on a lineage column IMPLIES a declared invalidator. This is the centroid defect made UNEXPRESSIBLE rather than merely visible.
MATERIALIZER / BACKFILL — replay declared (global) plus recovery.reset may not be "none".
RECORDER — outputs.publish required, and it may not be "none".
